statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across 274 clinical Mtb isolates, virulence gene expression varied more than expected, and that variation was tied to both known and previously unknown regulators.
statements.evidence: Across 274 Mtb clinical isolates, we uncovered unexpected diversity in virulence gene expression, which we linked to known and unknown regulators.
statements.note: The abstract reports exactly this for its panel of 274 clinical isolates.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Isolates carrying the low-expression variants grow faster in culture than isolates with normal EsxA and EsxB expression.
statements.evidence: Surprisingly, we found that many isolates harbor variants associated with decreased expression of EsxA (Esat6) and EsxB (Cfp10), which are virulence effectors, dominant T cell antigens, and immunodiagnostic targets.
statements.note: The abstract ties these variants to expression levels and to transmissibility, but never reports in vitro growth rates.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Many isolates harboured variants linked to reduced expression of EsxA and EsxB, two virulence effectors that also serve as immunodiagnostic targets.
statements.evidence: we found that many isolates harbor variants associated with decreased expression of EsxA (Esat6) and EsxB (Cfp10), which are virulence effectors, dominant T cell antigens, and immunodiagnostic targets
statements.note: The abstract states that many isolates carry such variants and describes these two proteins as immunodiagnostic targets.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In a set of more than 55,000 isolates, these variants went together with higher transmissibility, most markedly among drug-resistant strains.
statements.evidence: Across >55,000 isolates, these variants associate with increased transmissibility, especially in drug-resistant Mtb strains.
statements.note: The abstract reports this association and its concentration in drug-resistant strains.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The updated release contributes 1055 chimeric breakpoints obtained from public chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) datasets.
statements.evidence: This updated database provides unique information on 1055 chimeric breakpoints derived from public datasets using chromosome conformation capture techniques (the Hi-C datasets).
statements.note: The abstract gives this count and its Hi-C source directly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Chimeric breakpoint data in this release span 934 cell lines, which the resource offers for testing personalized cancer therapies.
statements.evidence: chimeric breakpoints across 934 cell lines, positioning ChiTaRS 8.0 as a valuable resource for testing personalized cancer therapies
statements.note: Both the cell-line count and the stated use for personalized therapy testing appear in the abstract.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Patient blood and plasma samples were among the sources mined to find previously unreported chimeras, including ones from oral squamous cell carcinoma and glioblastoma.
statements.evidence: as well as patient blood and plasma samples, we have identified novel chimeras
statements.note: The abstract lists patient blood and plasma among the inputs used to identify novel chimeras in these diseases.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Chimeric transcripts are more abundant in the plasma of glioblastoma patients than in the plasma of healthy donors.
statements.evidence: as well as patient blood and plasma samples, we have identified novel chimeras
statements.note: The abstract says novel chimeras were found and catalogued, but reports no abundance comparison between patients and healthy donors.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Amplification-free direct cDNA sequencing recovered more novel transcripts than PCR-amplified cDNA sequencing.
statements.evidence: We describe differences in read length, coverage, throughput and transcript expression, reporting that long-read RNA sequencing more robustly identifies major isoforms.
statements.note: The abstract treats long-read sequencing as a group and makes no protocol-by-protocol comparison for novel transcript discovery.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Seven human cell lines were profiled with five different RNA-sequencing protocols, with several spike-in controls included.
statements.evidence: we profiled seven human cell lines with five different RNA-sequencing protocols
statements.note: These counts and the spike-in controls are stated in the abstract's description of the design.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Major isoforms were identified more robustly by long-read RNA sequencing than by the other protocols profiled.
statements.evidence: reporting that long-read RNA sequencing more robustly identifies major isoforms
statements.note: This is the comparative result the abstract reports.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The protocols compared differed from one another in read length, coverage, throughput and the transcript expression they reported.
statements.evidence: We describe differences in read length, coverage, throughput and transcript expression
statements.note: The abstract names these four axes of difference.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The absolute concentration of cell-free microbial DNA in plasma was low relative to matched stool and saliva, yet significantly exceeded negative controls.
statements.evidence: Compared to matched stool and saliva samples, the absolute concentration of cfmDNA is low but significantly above the levels detected from negative controls.
statements.note: The abstract reports both halves of this comparison.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Contaminants from laboratory reagents and the DNA extraction and sequencing steps strongly shaped the microbial community recovered from plasma.
statements.evidence: The microbial community of plasma is strongly influenced by laboratory and reagent contaminants introduced during the DNA extraction and sequencing processes.
statements.note: The abstract states this influence explicitly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Levels of cell-free microbial DNA fall in melanoma patients after they start systemic therapy.
statements.evidence: We analyse additional plasma samples, highlighting the potential of this framework to identify differences in cfmDNA between healthy and cancer patients.
statements.note: The abstract mentions only differences between healthy and cancer groups and reports nothing about changes during treatment.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: After filtering batch-dependent sequence variants and those more prevalent in negative controls, known gut commensals such as Faecalibacterium, Bacteroides and Ruminococcus were detected.
statements.evidence: we identify known gut commensal bacteria, such as Faecalibacterium, Bacteroides and Ruminococcus, and also other uncharacterised ASVs
statements.note: These genera are the ones the abstract names as detected after its decontamination steps.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The dataset covers 189 patient tumours plus 41 matched normal samples, sequenced on the Oxford Nanopore PromethION platform.
statements.evidence: comprises a cohort of 189 patient tumors and 41 matched normal samples sequenced using the Oxford Nanopore Technologies PromethION platform
statements.note: Both sample counts and the platform are given in the abstract's opening sentence.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Long-read sequencing changed treatment decisions for patients whose short-read analysis had been uninformative.
statements.evidence: This dataset demonstrates applications for long-read sequencing in precision medicine and is available as a resource for developing analytical approaches using this technology.
statements.note: The abstract speaks of applications in precision medicine in general and reports no clinical decisions or patient outcomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Long-range phasing yielded allelically differentially methylated regions and allele-specific expression, with recurrent such regions in RET and CDKN2A.
statements.evidence: Long-range phasing facilitates the discovery of allelically differentially methylated regions (aDMRs) and allele-specific expression, including recurrent aDMRs in the cancer genes RET and CDKN2A.
statements.note: The abstract names these two genes as carrying recurrent aDMRs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Where no coding driver mutation was found, promoter methylation of BRCA1 and RAD51C was the probable cause of homologous recombination deficiency.
statements.evidence: Promoter methylation in BRCA1 and RAD51C is a likely driver behind homologous recombination deficiency where no coding driver mutation was found.
statements.note: This restates the abstract's conclusion about methylation-driven homologous recombination deficiency.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Oesophageal epithelioids kept themselves going for a year or more without passaging while staying genomically stable.
statements.evidence: Esophageal epithelioids self-maintain without passaging for at least 1 year, maintaining a three-dimensional structure with proliferative basal cells that differentiate into suprabasal cells, which eventually shed and retain genomic stability.
statements.note: The abstract states the one-year self-maintenance and the retention of genomic stability in the same sentence.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Live imaging across five months showed that the cultures reproduce cell dynamics observed in vivo.
statements.evidence: Live imaging over 5 months showed that epithelioids replicate in vivo cell dynamics.
statements.note: The abstract reports this imaging result and its duration.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A targeted CRISPR-Cas9 screen reproduced the mutant gene selection seen in ageing human oesophagus and uncovered further drivers of clonal expansion.
statements.evidence: a targeted CRISPR-Cas9 screen shows that epithelioids recapitulate mutant gene selection in aging human esophagus and identifies additional drivers of clonal expansion
statements.note: The abstract reports both the recapitulation and the newly identified drivers.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mutant clones that expand in epithelioids go on to form invasive tumours when the cultures are kept beyond one year.
statements.evidence: Epithelioids support genetic manipulation and enable the study of mutant cell competition and selection in three-dimensional epithelia, and show how anti-cancer treatments modulate competition between transformed and wild-type cells.
statements.note: The abstract covers competition between transformed and wild-type cells but says nothing about progression to invasive tumours.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: SaferSeqS detected residual disease in post-surgical plasma earlier than imaging did.
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that it can evaluate mutations in a single amplicon or simultaneously in multiple amplicons, assess limited quantities of cell-free DNA with high recovery of both strands
statements.note: The abstract reports assay performance characteristics only, with no patient follow-up and no comparison against imaging.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The method picks up variants present at frequencies below one in 100,000 DNA template molecules.
statements.evidence: detects variants at frequencies below 1 in 100,000 DNA template molecules
statements.note: This detection limit is stated outright in the abstract.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Error rates were cut more than a hundredfold relative to existing PCR-based molecular barcoding approaches.
statements.evidence: reduce the error rate of existing PCR-based molecular barcoding approaches by >100-fold
statements.note: The abstract quantifies the improvement over prior barcoding methods as greater than 100-fold.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The approach works on small amounts of cell-free DNA and recovers both strands of the template molecules at high rates.
statements.evidence: assess limited quantities of cell-free DNA with high recovery of both strands
statements.note: The abstract lists this among the demonstrated capabilities.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The assay resolves six active and repressive histone modifications, together with their ratios and combinatorial patterns, across millions of single nucleosomes.
statements.evidence: high-resolution detection of six active and repressive histone modifications and their ratios and combinatorial patterns on millions of individual nucleosomes by single-molecule imaging
statements.note: The abstract states the number of modifications and the single-molecule scale.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Plasma from 63 colorectal cancer, 10 pancreatic cancer and 33 healthy donors was classified accurately, including at early disease stages.
statements.evidence: EPINUC analysis of a cohort of 63 colorectal cancer, 10 pancreatic cancer and 33 healthy plasma samples detected cancer with high accuracy and sensitivity, even at early stages.
statements.note: The cohort composition and the early-stage detection claim are both in the abstract.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The assay separated colorectal from pancreatic cancer more accurately than carcinoembryonic antigen measurement.
statements.evidence: EPINUC analysis of a cohort of 63 colorectal cancer, 10 pancreatic cancer and 33 healthy plasma samples detected cancer with high accuracy and sensitivity, even at early stages.
statements.note: The abstract reports detection and tissue of origin but makes no comparison with conventional protein tumour markers.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Adding direct single-molecule DNA sequencing to the assay revealed the tissue of origin of colorectal, pancreatic, lung and breast tumours.
statements.evidence: combining EPINUC with direct single-molecule DNA sequencing revealed the tissue of origin of colorectal, pancreatic, lung and breast tumors
statements.note: The abstract names these four tumour types for the tissue-of-origin result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Testing at cycle 1 day 1 flagged 214 of the evaluable patients, 37%, as ctDNA-positive, and these patients had poor prognosis.
statements.evidence: ctDNA testing at the start of therapy (cycle 1 day 1) identified 214 (37%) patients who were positive for ctDNA and who had poor prognosis
statements.note: The abstract gives this count, proportion and prognostic finding.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Clearance of ctDNA by week 6 occurred in 18% of patients on atezolizumab against 4% under observation.
statements.evidence: The rate of ctDNA clearance at week 6 was higher in the atezolizumab arm (18%) than in the observation arm (4%)
statements.note: Both clearance rates are reported in the abstract.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among ctDNA-negative patients, neither disease-free survival nor overall survival differed between the atezolizumab and observation arms.
statements.evidence: No difference in disease-free survival or overall survival between treatment arms was noted for patients who were negative for ctDNA.
statements.note: The abstract states this null result for the ctDNA-negative subgroup.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: ctDNA-positive patients carried a higher tumour mutational burden than ctDNA-negative patients.
statements.evidence: Transcriptomic analysis of tumours from patients who were positive for ctDNA revealed higher expression levels of cell-cycle and keratin genes.
statements.note: The abstract reports transcriptomic differences between these groups and says nothing about mutational burden.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Aligning to the complete CHM13-T2T reference improved structural variant detection accuracy over GRCh38, with a marked drop in false-positive calls.
statements.evidence: show that the CHM13-T2T improves SV detection accuracy compared to GRCh38 with a notable reduction in false-positive calls
statements.note: This is the comparative result reported for the benchmark and patient samples.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The gain in accuracy from CHM13-T2T was largest for structural variants in centromeric and segmentally duplicated regions.
statements.evidence: Our findings in a tumor-normal matched benchmark sample and three patient samples show that the CHM13-T2T improves SV detection accuracy compared to GRCh38 with a notable reduction in false-positive calls, and thus supports improved prioritization.
statements.note: The abstract reports an overall accuracy improvement without breaking it down by genomic region.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across four COLO829 replicates, 346 structural variants, or 1.13%, appeared in only one replicate, while 54 somatic variants were present in all four.
statements.evidence: 346 SVs (1.13%) were only discoverable in a single replicate. We identify 54 somatic SVs, which appear to be stable as they are consistently present across the four replicates.
statements.note: Both counts come from the abstract's assessment of replicate instability.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Reads aligned to CHM13-T2T were lifted over to GRCh38, combining the better alignment with the richer annotation resources available for that reference.
statements.evidence: We also overcame the lack of annotation resources for CHM13-T2T by lifting over CHM13-T2T-aligned reads to the GRCh38 genome, therefore combining both improved alignment and advanced annotations.
statements.note: The abstract describes exactly this liftover strategy and its purpose.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The A7 element raises mRNA stability whether it is inserted at the 5' or the 3' end of the transcript.
statements.evidence: An element named A7 demonstrates particularly robust performance across cell types, delivery methods, modifications and coding sequences, making linear mRNA as stable as circular RNA while achieving higher translation efficiency.
statements.note: The abstract lists the contexts in which A7 proved robust but never says where in the transcript the element sits.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A screen of 196,277 viral sequences yielded eleven elements that strongly increase both mRNA stability and translation.
statements.evidence: we screen 196,277 viral sequences and identify eleven elements that strongly enhance mRNA stability and translation
statements.note: The abstract gives the number of sequences screened and the number of elements recovered.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The elements work by recruiting TENT4 to lengthen the poly(A) tail, which blocks deadenylation.
statements.evidence: Mechanistically, they recruit TENT4 to extend the poly(A) tail, preventing deadenylation.
statements.note: This is the mechanism the abstract reports.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In mouse liver, linear mRNA carrying A7 gave substantially higher protein levels than circular RNA, with expression lasting beyond two weeks.
statements.evidence: In mouse liver, A7-containing linear mRNA exhibits substantially higher protein levels than circular RNA, with sustained expression lasting for over 2 weeks.
statements.note: The abstract reports this in vivo comparison and its duration.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In a newly generated set of 14,994 non-small cell lung cancer cells from matched primary and metastatic sites, proliferation differed widely between clones.
statements.evidence: Applied to a newly generated longitudinal, primary-metastasis-matched dataset of 14,994 non-small cell lung cancer cells, SPRINTER revealed widespread clone proliferation heterogeneity
statements.note: The abstract gives this cell count and reports widespread proliferation heterogeneity between clones.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Clones with high proliferation showed greater metastatic seeding potential and shed more circulating tumour DNA.
statements.evidence: high-proliferation clones have increased metastatic seeding potential, increased circulating tumor DNA shedding
statements.note: Both properties are attributed to high-proliferation clones in the abstract.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients whose tumours contained high-proliferation clones had shorter overall survival than patients without them.

statements.note: The abstract links high-proliferation clones to seeding, shedding and replication timing, but reports no patient survival data.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In 61,914 previously published breast and ovarian cancer cells, high-proliferation clones were enriched for amplifications of proliferation-related genes.
statements.evidence: Applied to previously generated datasets of 61,914 breast and ovarian cancer cells, SPRINTER revealed increased single-cell rates of different genomic variants and enrichment of proliferation-related gene amplifications in high-proliferation clones.
statements.note: The abstract reports this enrichment in the re-analysed breast and ovarian datasets.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In healthy individuals, the short double-stranded cfDNA fraction showed significant enrichment of 203 transcription factor motifs.
statements.evidence: In short double-stranded cfDNA from healthy individuals, we find significant enrichment of 203 transcription factor motifs.
statements.note: The abstract gives this motif count for healthy individuals.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: At particular genomic regions the short double-stranded cfDNA signal ran opposite to DNA methylation and in the same direction as H3K4me3 and transcription.
statements.evidence: short double-stranded cfDNA signals at specific genomic regions correlate negatively with DNA methylation, positively with H3K4me3 histone modifications and gene transcription

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Comparisons yielded 136 differentially enriched loci between pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and colorectal carcinoma and 241 between septic and postoperative controls.
statements.evidence: When comparing short double-stranded cfDNA from patient samples of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with colorectal carcinoma or septic with postoperative controls, we identify 136 and 241 differentially enriched loci, respectively.

statements.text: Loss of SET-24 raised H3K4me3 at the transcription start sites of hundreds of genes.

statements.text: Proteomic, yeast two-hybrid and pull-down assays all showed SET-24 binding the chromatin factor HCF-1.
statements.evidence: Proteomic, yeast two-hybrid, and pull-down assays show that SET-24 interacts with HCF-1, a chromatin factor linked to complexes like COMPASS, which deposits H3K4me3.

statements.text: Transcription stayed largely unchanged in the mutants, yet small RNA production was disrupted for roughly 30% of the affected genes.
statements.evidence: Although transcription remains largely unchanged, small RNA production is disrupted for about 30% of these genes.

statements.evidence: LasiRNA biogenesis relied on RNA-dependent RNA polymerases and Dicer-like proteins (DCLs).

statements.text: With pathogen infection and DBR1 dysfunction, DCL4 and DCL2 processed many lariat RNAs into siRNAs directed at immunity genes, which disrupted defense responses.
statements.evidence: Upon pathogen infection and dysfunction of DBR1, many lariat RNAs were hijacked by DCL4 and DCL2 and processed into siRNAs that particularly target immunity genes, ultimately disrupting plant defense responses.
